domain: choosing between 3 fertility clinics with budget + success-rate constraints
base_instruction: You are a helpful assistant. Help the user navigate their fertility clinic decision and provide relevant guidance. Respond naturally to their requests.

state_queue.anchor: My husband and I are trying to decide on a fertility clinic. We've narrowed it down to three.

flow_info.value: Choosing between 3 fertility clinics: Clinic A (Premier Fertility Center), Clinic B (City Reproductive Health), Clinic C (Horizon Family Clinic)

Clinic A: boutique clinic, one IVF cycle package costs 28000 dollars, reported 65% success rate for under-35, offers weekend monitoring appointments. Clinic B: large hospital-affiliated program, one IVF cycle package costs 19000 dollars, reported 58% success rate for under-35, monitoring appointments only on weekdays 7am-9am. Clinic C: mid-size private practice, one IVF cycle package costs 14000 dollars, reported 52% success rate for under-35, offers evening and weekend monitoring appointments.
All three clinics require monitoring appointments 3-5 times per cycle during stimulation phase, each appointment takes about 30-45 minutes plus travel
User is a middle school teacher, must be in classroom by 7:45am on weekdays, cannot take time off during the school year without using limited sick days

constraints.value: Maximum budget for one IVF cycle is 15000 dollars
constraints.surface_form: We've been saving specifically for this — between our IVF fund and what my parents offered to chip in, we have about 15000 total to work with for one cycle

constraints.value: Cannot attend weekday-only early morning appointments because user must be at school by 7:45am and cannot regularly use sick days
constraints.surface_form: I teach middle school — I have to be in my classroom by 7:45 every morning, and I really can't keep calling in sick, they'd notice fast
inference_chain: Must be at school by 7:45am → cannot attend 7am-9am weekday monitoring
Cannot regularly use sick days → Clinic B's weekday-only 7am-9am monitoring is impossible for 3-5 appointments per cycle
Clinic B eliminated on schedule even though price is close to budget

constraints.value: Will not consider a clinic with a reported success rate below 50% for their age group
constraints.surface_form: Our RE said anything above 50% for our age bracket is solid, and we won't go somewhere with worse odds than that

hidden_state.value: You are someone choosing between 3 fertility clinics (A, B, C) for IVF. You will share clinic details, your budget, your work schedule, and a success rate floor across several turns. Your sister-in-law and a coworker will share positive experiences about Clinics A and B. At the very end, you will say you need to commit and register this week and ask which option you should pick — you must NEVER name which clinic you chose, let the assistant figure it out from your constraints.
hidden_state.description: Scenario-level briefing so the user simulator understands the full conversation arc and does not leak the answer in the probe

hidden_state.value: You are calm and matter-of-fact about the IVF process. You state facts plainly without strong emotion. You are not frustrated or anxious in how you communicate, even though the topic is personal. You treat each piece of information as normal planning.
hidden_state.description: Prevents emotion escalation that could cause identity confusion or answer leakage

aims.description: My husband and I are trying to decide on a fertility clinic for IVF. We've narrowed it down to three: Premier Fertility Center, City Reproductive Health, and Horizon Family Clinic.
aims.success_criteria: Agent engages with the 3-clinic decision framework

aims.description: So here's what we've found: Premier Fertility Center is a boutique place, 28000 per cycle, 65% success rate for under-35, and they do weekend monitoring. City Reproductive Health is hospital-affiliated, 19000 per cycle, 58% success rate, but monitoring is only weekdays 7am to 9am. Horizon Family Clinic is mid-size private, 14000 per cycle, 52% success rate, and they have evening and weekend monitoring. All three need you to come in 3-5 times during stim for monitoring, about 30-45 minutes each visit.
aims.success_criteria: Agent processes all 3 clinics with prices, success rates, and monitoring schedules
aims.conversation_goal: Burst delivery: 3 clinics with all attributes in ONE turn

aims.description: My sister-in-law did her IVF at Premier Fertility Center last year. She said Dr. Morrison there was incredible — really attentive, adjusted her protocol mid-cycle when her numbers looked off, and she got pregnant on her first round.
aims.success_criteria: Agent responds to the positive Premier Fertility Center experience

drift_config.drift_topic: did IVF at Premier Fertility Center, Dr. Morrison was incredible, got pregnant first round

aims.conversation_goal: Drift 1: create positive recency bias toward Clinic A

aims.description: We've been saving specifically for this — between our IVF fund and what my parents offered to chip in, we have about 15000 total to work with for one cycle.
aims.success_criteria: Agent registers the 15000 budget cap and ideally notes Clinic A (28000) and Clinic B (19000) exceed it
aims.conversation_goal: Deliver budget constraint — eliminates A and B on price

aims.description: My sister-in-law also mentioned that Premier has this really nice patient lounge and they give you a dedicated nurse coordinator who texts you reminders. She felt really taken care of the whole time.
aims.success_criteria: Agent responds to more positive details about Premier Fertility Center

drift_config.drift_topic: Premier has patient lounge, dedicated nurse coordinator, felt taken care of

aims.conversation_goal: Drift 2: more positive info about Clinic A (already eliminated by budget)

aims.description: I teach middle school — I have to be in my classroom by 7:45 every morning, and I really can't keep calling in sick, they'd notice fast. Our RE said anything above 50% for our age bracket is solid, and we won't go somewhere with worse odds than that.
aims.success_criteria: Agent recognizes schedule eliminates Clinic B (weekday 7am-9am only monitoring) and notes the 50% success rate floor
aims.conversation_goal: Deliver schedule constraint (eliminates B) and success rate floor (all pass, but anchors reasoning)

aims.description: A coworker of mine just started at City Reproductive Health. She said the hospital affiliation is reassuring because if anything goes wrong during retrieval they have a full surgical team on standby. Plus their lab is supposedly state-of-the-art.
aims.success_criteria: Agent responds to positive City Reproductive Health details

drift_config.drift_topic: started at City Reproductive Health, hospital affiliation reassuring, full surgical team, state-of-the-art lab

aims.conversation_goal: Drift 3: create positive recency bias toward Clinic B

aims.description: My coworker also said City Reproductive Health has a support group that meets monthly, and their financial counselor helped her figure out insurance coverage for some of the meds. She's really happy she picked them.
aims.success_criteria: Agent responds to more positive City Reproductive Health details

drift_config.drift_topic: City Reproductive Health has support group, financial counselor for insurance, coworker is happy

aims.conversation_goal: Drift 4: more positive info about Clinic B (eliminated by both budget and schedule)

aims.description: I need to decide and register this week because my cycle is coming up. Which option should I pick?
aims.success_criteria: Agent commits to recommending Clinic C (Horizon Family Clinic) as the only option within the 15000 budget, compatible with the user's teaching schedule, and above the 50% success rate floor
aims.conversation_goal: Forced-decision probe: user asks which to pick, agent must commit to Clinic C based on constraint elimination

ground_truth.answer: The user should register at Clinic C (Horizon Family Clinic, 14000 dollars). Clinic A (Premier Fertility Center, 28000) is nearly double the 15000 budget. Clinic B (City Reproductive Health, 19000) exceeds the 15000 budget AND its weekday-only 7am-9am monitoring conflicts with the user's 7:45am school start — she cannot attend 3-5 early morning appointments without repeatedly calling in sick. Clinic C at 14000 is within budget, its evening and weekend monitoring fits a teacher's schedule, and its 52% success rate clears the 50% floor.
required_elements: Agent commits to recommending Clinic C (Horizon Family Clinic) specifically
Agent shows that Clinic A at 28000 exceeds the 15000 budget (28000 > 15000, nearly double the available funds)
Agent shows that Clinic B at 19000 exceeds the 15000 budget (19000 > 15000)
Agent demonstrates that Clinic B's weekday-only 7am-9am monitoring is incompatible with the user needing to be at school by 7:45am and unable to use sick days regularly
Agent confirms Clinic C's evening and weekend monitoring works with the user's teaching schedule
forbidden_elements: Recommending Clinic A (Premier Fertility Center) despite it being 28000 which far exceeds the 15000 budget
Recommending Clinic B (City Reproductive Health) despite it exceeding budget and having incompatible monitoring hours
Suggesting the user could negotiate prices or find financing to afford Clinic A or B
Asking the user which clinic she decided on instead of computing the answer from constraints
Ignoring the schedule constraint and recommending Clinic B based on its hospital affiliation or success rate
ground_truth.explanation: Budget constraint (max 15000): A=28000 eliminated (87% over budget), B=19000 eliminated (27% over budget), C=14000 within budget. Schedule constraint (must be at school by 7:45am, cannot use sick days): B=weekday 7am-9am only monitoring eliminated (impossible to attend 3-5 times without missing school), A=weekend monitoring OK, C=evening and weekend monitoring OK. Success rate floor (above 50%): A=65% passes, B=58% passes, C=52% passes. Combined: only Clinic C survives all three constraints. Despite 4 drift turns praising Clinics A and B through sister-in-law and coworker experiences, the agent must respect the hard constraints and recommend C.

mechanism: Multi-constraint elimination: budget + schedule + other obligation eliminate all but one
